title: Adic quotients of a finite-type localization are unchanged after completing the local base
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring (local means having the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/\mathfrak m^n$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion with canonical map $\iota:R\to\widehat R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $C$ be a finite-type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $C$ containing $\mathfrak mC$. Put $D=C\otimes_R\widehat R$ [def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(c\otimes a)(c'\otimes a')=cc'\otimes aa'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and structural maps $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. If $Q$ is a prime ideal of $D$ whose contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak q$ and whose contraction to $\widehat R$ is its maximal ideal, then for every $n\geq1$ the canonical local map $C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] induces an isomorphism
$$C_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q})^n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Q/(QD_Q)^n.$$
These isomorphisms commute with the quotient transition maps for all $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00MA(3), together with the finite-type affine localization and quotient calculation written in the proof of this node

proof.text: Write $f:C\to D$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, its ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. For each $n\geq1$, apply the completion-mod-power statement to $(R,\mathfrak m)$: the projection $\pi_n:\widehat R\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ is a surjective $R$-algebra map, $\pi_n\iota$ is reduction, and $\ker\pi_n=\mathfrak m^n\widehat R$. Also $\widehat R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat R$ by the local-completion statement. Thus all these assertions apply to the particular completion in the hypotheses.

For each $n\geq1$, apply [lem-trf-tensor-base-change-ideal-power-quotients] with $I=\mathfrak m$, $J=\mathfrak q$, $B=\widehat R$, and $\pi=\pi_n$ from Step 1. The containment $IC\subseteq J$ is the assumed $\mathfrak mC\subseteq\mathfrak q$; the projection, reduction and kernel hypotheses were verified in Step 1. Consequently $f:C\to D$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, induces a ring isomorphism $\alpha_n:C/\mathfrak q^n\xrightarrow{\sim}D/\mathfrak q^nD$ for every positive $n$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product): universal property and bilinear-relations construction; explicit ring-quotient inverse argument extracted from returned item Steps 2-3, with the finite-level scalar congruence taken as a hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-adic-quotient-isomorphisms-localize] to $f:C\to D$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q$ and the given prime $Q$. Its contraction hypothesis is exactly the assumed $f^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak q$, and its canonical global quotient isomorphisms are those of Step 2. It gives $Q=\mathfrak qD$ and ring isomorphisms $e_n:C_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q})^n\to D_Q/(QD_Q)^n$ with $e_n([c/s])=[f(c)/f(s)]$, induced by the canonical local map. For $k\geq n\geq1$, both transition composites send $[c/s]$ to $[f(c)/f(s)]$ at exponent $n$; every source class has such a representative. Thus the specified canonical isomorphisms commute with every quotient transition map, proving both clauses.
